name: PPPP Active Runtime Manifest

statusDefinitions.BASE_DIRECT: Loaded directly by the application HTML before the additive runtime bootstrap. It may be foundational without owning the final visible UI.
statusDefinitions.FOUNDATION_REQUIRED: Current foundational shell or host layer required by later runtime owners. It may be visually superseded while still providing DOM, classes, globals or lifecycle hooks that later modules depend on.
statusDefinitions.FINAL_OWNER: Known current owner/finalizer for a visible runtime area. Later modules may still decorate it.
statusDefinitions.COMPATIBILITY: Required bridge, adapter, safety wrapper or migration layer. Do not infer UI ownership from this file.
statusDefinitions.LOADED_LEGACY_CANDIDATE: Still loaded in production but likely superseded in visible behavior. Must not be removed until callers, globals, events and smoke tests are traced.
statusDefinitions.LEGACY_FALLBACK_REQUIRED: Legacy layer intentionally retained because a current user-accessible fallback still depends on its behavior. Do not retire it until that fallback is removed or replaced.
statusDefinitions.ACTIVE_PROVIDER: Conditionally active runtime provider loaded outside the main bootstrap.
statusDefinitions.DYNAMIC_CURRENT: Current production module loaded dynamically by another current runtime file rather than by the main bootstrap.
statusDefinitions.LOADED_CURRENT_UNCLASSIFIED: Loaded by the production bootstrap and therefore treated as required until explicitly classified.

areas.note: Workspace Architecture provides the shell. Native UI v3 is the early presentation owner. Operating Experience remains the cross-area desktop presentation/navigation owner. Mobile Responsive v1 is a <=900px presentation/navigation-only shell that reuses canonical routes, adds no Supabase reads/writes or polling, and leaves business/data ownership unchanged. UI Runtime Stability observes route settling without cloning pages, duplicating ids, intercepting clicks or owning routing. Mobile PIN Unlock v1 is a device-local <=900px quick-unlock layer over an already valid remembered Supabase session. It stores no plaintext PIN or password, adds no Supabase/network reads, and falls back to full login when the session is unavailable or after repeated failures. RBAC startup now keeps role resolution bound to the authenticated identity in standalone PWA mode and never converts a transient startup delay into Viewer; exact-email fallback is allowed only after an authenticated user_id row miss. SPIE standard CSS owns desktop shell geometry on the static pst-spie-standard root. Existing canonical modules retain actions/data; legacy geometry writers defer. Home typography also owns nested module roots. Representations uses one contextual left column with branch navigation and filters; existing business owners are unchanged.

Desktop Home has one visual owner: pristeel-home-launcher-v4.js. Native UI and Redesign Finalizer defer legacy child retirement when the launcher is present. The launcher clears inherited hidden/aria-hidden state, hides all legacy Home children, ignores stale Home nav markers, and owns the sidebar boundary via pst-home-shell-owned. Home has no sidebar or reserved width; its four primary module routes restore canonical navigation. Global/Production shell owners defer only within this boundary, while other routes retain their existing full-width behavior. Gazeta PPPP remains an in-Home overlay and the duplicate floating Daily launcher stays hidden. Route/render events are coalesced and reuse successful weather data until explicit refresh. In SPIE standard mode the launcher keeps the same handlers but uses calm module rows with a persistent sidebar.

Projects Operator Desk v2 remains the main Projects owner. The RFQ & Sourcing companion adds only Oltian's assigned open-task queue and routes each row into the existing Project workspace; it does not create another project lifecycle or status engine.

Project Integrity UI owns the bounded base project load. Canonical Project Workflow remains the navigation/business-route owner. Project Workbench v3 is the exclusive visible Project Detail presentation owner. RFQ & Sourcing reuses its dossier, requirement extraction, RFQ draft, supplier quotation and comparison surfaces; the multi-supplier package plan is an internal, explicitly human-approved cost composition only. Technical documentation stays manual. No companion performs automatic outbound communication, supplier commitment, pricing approval or PO creation.
Contact Master is the final relationship register.

Legacy dach-steel filename is retained for compatibility. The visible owner is Material Trade across EU + CH + ME + RS: Tier 1 direct steel consumers/fabricators/manufacturers, Tier 2 construction/GC-GU only with steel-procurement evidence. Buyer rows surface company intelligence, steel scope, public contact evidence and source links; a named project is optional and never invented. Lifecycle is ready-to-contact → Gmail draft → sent/waiting → replied/active → human-confirmed trading Project, while discovery/runtime remains explicitly separate from TED/Mundësitë.

Kompanitë EU është pipeline-i i veçantë për klientë të drejtpërdrejtë në Evropë për paketa çeliku të fabrikuar, kapacitet prodhues dhe nënkontraktim. Përjashton Mundësitë/tenderët, blerësit e lëndës së parë te Blerësit e çelikut dhe targetet e Përfaqësimeve. Lexon kontrollet globale të identitetit dhe historikut të kontaktimit, por nuk dërgon email dhe nuk krijon projekt automatikisht.

Tender discovery engines remain backstage. Project-Centric Workflow remains the visible Opportunities owner. The dossier analyzer owns public/partial dossier reading; protected KRPP documents are imported through the existing protected_archive. Tender Supplier Sourcing provides evidence-ranked candidates; Arianit explicitly shortlists RFQ-ready suppliers and hands one canonical task to Oltian only after the tender is a Project. No tender becomes a project, no supplier is committed, and no RFQ/email is sent without a human decision.
AI providers remain explicit and human-triggered.
